lem-qa-15-continuous-markov-derivative-b:
## Statement

If $p$ is a real polynomial with no supported monomial of degree greater than $d\in\mathbb N_0$, and $h:=\max_{[-1,1]}p-\min_{[-1,1]}p$, then
$$\max_{[-1,1]}|p'|\le \frac{d^2h}{2}.$$
The zero polynomial is allowed under the support-degree convention.
lem-qa-15-grid-return-derivative:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and let $q$ be a real polynomial. On $[0,N]$, set
$$h:=\max q-\min q,\qquad D:=\max |q'|.$$
If $0\le q(k)\le1$ for every integer $k=0,\ldots,N$, then
$$D\ge \max\{0,h-1\}.$$
lem-qa-15-discrete-markov-ehlich-zeller:
## Statement

Let $N\ge1$ and let $q$ be a real polynomial with no supported monomial of degree greater than $d\in\mathbb N_0$. Put $h=\max_{[0,N]}q-\min_{[0,N]}q$ and $D=\max_{[0,N]}|q'|$. If $0\le q(k)\le1$ for every integer $k=0,\ldots,N$, then
$$D\le\frac{d^2}{N}h.$$
def-qa-15-bit-oracle-query-model:
## Definition

Fix an integer $N\ge0$ and a promise domain $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^N$ as in [[def-qa-task-and-promise-domain]]. For each full-cube input $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1})$, define the total address function $g_x:\{0,1\}^N\to\{0,1\}$ by $g_x(e_i)=x_i$ for the one-hot word $e_i$ ($0\le i<N$), and $g_x(a)=0$ for every other address. If $N=0$, the address set has only the empty word and $g_x$ is identically zero. A **local bit-query algorithm** is a finite rooted execution tree on one fixed finite ordered register, starting in the all-zero computational-basis state $|0^m\rangle$ for its fixed register length $m$. The tree topology and each node label are fixed independently of $x$. Each non-oracle node is either a fixed unitary or a fixed finite instrument, with its observed outcomes retained for later control; every such operation is independent of $x$. Each query node acts on a declared $N$-bit address register and a disjoint one-bit target register by the standard XOR oracle $U_{g_x}$ of [[def-qa-standard-bit-query]], tensored with the identity on all other wires. Every terminal node uses the same ordered output-wire tuple and the same fixed accepting subset $S\subseteq\{0,1\}^r$, independent of $x$; the output law sums over all unmeasured labels and all terminal branch histories as in [[def-qa-finite-branch-output-law]].

The **query count of a branch** is the number of query nodes on its root-to-terminal path. The algorithm makes at most $T$ queries when every such path contains at most $T$ query nodes. A local bit-query algorithm has **no direct input access**: there is no input register containing $x$, no $x$-dependent non-oracle operation or initial state, and no $x$-dependent terminal predicate. Thus $x$ enters only through the stated bit oracle. This is the oracle-only specialization used for the QA15 polynomial-method results.
def-qa-15-acceptance-polynomial:
## Definition

For a local bit-query algorithm $A$ on $N$ input bits, an **acceptance polynomial** is a real polynomial $p(X_0,\ldots,X_{N-1})$ such that $p(x)=\Pr[A\text{ accepts }x]$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^N$. The probability is the finite output law of [[def-qa-15-bit-oracle-query-model]].

For a promise function $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ with $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^N$ and $\epsilon\ge0$, a polynomial $p$ is an **$\epsilon$-approximant on $D$** if $|p(x)-f(x)|\le\epsilon$ for every $x\in D$. Its **total degree is at most $d$** when each monomial with nonzero coefficient has total degree at most $d$. This support convention includes the zero polynomial at every $d\ge0$, although the formal zero polynomial has no degree ([[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]]).

The **$\epsilon$-approximate degree** $\widetilde{\deg}_{\epsilon}(f;D)$ is the least $d\in\mathbb N_0$ for which some real polynomial of total degree at most $d$ is an $\epsilon$-approximant on $D$. This minimum exists: for $y\in\{0,1\}^N$ set $\delta_y(X)=\prod_{i<N}(y_iX_i+(1-y_i)(1-X_i))$. For Boolean $x$, each factor is $1$ exactly when $x_i=y_i$ and otherwise is $0$, so $\delta_y(x)=1$ exactly for $x=y$. Therefore $p_D(X)=\sum_{y\in D}f(y)\delta_y(X)$ equals $f$ on $D$ and has degree at most $N$; if $D=\varnothing$, the empty sum is zero and is vacuously an approximant. The admissible degree bounds in $\{0,\ldots,N\}$ form a nonempty finite set (it contains $N$), so it has a least element by [[lem-finite-set-has-max]] applied to its negatives. No choice principle is used.
def-qa-15-bit-oracle-query-complexity:
## Definition

Let $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ be a promise function and $0\le\epsilon<1/2$. Its **local bounded-error bit-query complexity** is
$$Q^{\mathrm{bit}}_{\epsilon}(f;D):=\min\{T\in\mathbb N_0:\text{some local bit-query algorithm making at most }T\text{ queries has }|\Pr[A\text{ accepts }x]-f(x)|\le\epsilon\text{ for every }x\in D\}.$$
The feasible set is nonempty. Query the one-hot addresses $e_0,\ldots,e_{N-1}$ in order, measuring each target bit and copying its result to a fresh, initially zero output wire by a fixed outcome-controlled bit flip; the outcomes are deterministically $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}$. Fixed branch operations reset the target between calls and set the next one-hot address, so the terminal output tuple is exactly the recorded $N$-bit word. The fixed terminal accepting subset $\{y\in D:f(y)=1\}$ then accepts exactly on yes-inputs in $D$, so this is an exact $N$-query algorithm (for $N=0$, the fixed output predicate suffices without a query). Thus the minimum is finite and at most $N$; it exists because the feasible counts below this one form a nonempty finite set of naturals, which has a least element by [[lem-finite-set-has-max]] applied to their negatives. The query count is the minimum worst-branch query count and does not charge non-oracle operations. “Local” refers exactly to the oracle-only interface in [[def-qa-15-bit-oracle-query-model]]. If $D=\varnothing$, a zero-query algorithm is feasible and the minimum is $0$.
lem-qa-15-branch-density-degree:
## Statement

Let $A$ be a local bit-query algorithm, allowing finite input-independent instrument branches, and let $h$ be any execution history containing $t(h)$ oracle calls. Write $\sigma_h(x):=w_h(x)\rho_h(x)$ for the unnormalized branch operator: $w_h$ is the probability weight of the history and $\rho_h$ its conditional density operator when $w_h>0$; set $\sigma_h=0$ when $w_h=0$. In the fixed computational basis, every matrix entry of $\sigma_h(x)$ on $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ is represented by a complex polynomial whose support has no monomial of total degree greater than $2t(h)$.
lem-qa-15-query-amplitude-degree:
## Statement

Let $A$ be a local bit-query algorithm on $N$ input bits whose non-oracle steps are all fixed unitaries, and suppose every execution uses at most $T$ queries. For each computational-basis state $|a,b,w\rangle$ of its fixed register, its amplitude after every circuit prefix is represented on the Boolean input cube by a complex polynomial in $X_0,\ldots,X_{N-1}$ whose support has no monomial of total degree greater than the number of queries in that prefix (and at the end none has degree greater than $T$).
lem-qa-15-symmetrization:
## Statement

Let $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^N$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and let $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ satisfy $f(\pi x)=f(x)$ for every permutation $\pi$ and $x\in D$. If a real polynomial $p$ of total degree at most $d$ is an $\epsilon$-approximant to $f$ on $D$, then there is a univariate real polynomial $q(t)$ of degree at most $d$ such that $q(|x|)$ is also an $\epsilon$-approximant on $D$, where $|x|:=\sum_{i<N}x_i$ is Hamming weight.
prop-qa-15-promise-domain-scope:
## Statement

For $f:D\to\{0,1\}$, the condition that a polynomial $p$ is an $\epsilon$-approximant means exactly $|p(x)-f(x)|\le\epsilon$ for $x\in D$; it imposes no condition at inputs outside $D$. If $D\subsetneq\{0,1\}^N$, then for every $y\notin D$ and every polynomial $p$, there is another polynomial agreeing with $p$ on $D$ and having a different value at $y$.
thm-qa-15-acceptance-degree-bound:
## Statement

If a local bit-query algorithm makes at most $T$ queries on every branch, then its full-cube acceptance probability $P_A(x)$ is represented on $\{0,1\}^N$ by a real multilinear polynomial of total degree at most $2T$. Consequently, if it computes $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ with error at most $\epsilon$ on a promise domain $D$, then $\widetilde{\deg}_{\epsilon}(f;D)\le2T$ and
$$Q^{\mathrm{bit}}_{\epsilon}(f;D)\ge\left\lceil\frac{\widetilde{\deg}_{\epsilon}(f;D)}2\right\rceil.$$
thm-qa-15-exact-degree-or:
## Statement

For $N\ge1$, let $\mathrm{OR}_N(x)=0$ when $x=0^N$ and $1$ otherwise. Its exact approximate degree is
$$\widetilde{\deg}_0(\mathrm{OR}_N;\{0,1\}^N)=N.$$
thm-qa-15-or-approximate-degree-lower-bo:
## Statement

For $N\ge1$, define $\mathrm{OR}_N(x)=0$ at $x=0^N$ and $1$ at every other Boolean vector. For $0\le\epsilon<1/2$ and $d=\widetilde{\deg}_{\epsilon}(\mathrm{OR}_N;\{0,1\}^N)$,
$$d^2\ge\frac{1-2\epsilon}{2}N.$$
Consequently every local bit-query algorithm computing OR with error at most $\epsilon$ has at least $\lceil d/2\rceil$ queries, and
$$Q^{\mathrm{bit}}_{\epsilon}(\mathrm{OR}_N;\{0,1\}^N)\ge\left\lceil\frac12\sqrt{\frac{1-2\epsilon}{2}N}\right\rceil.$$
thm-qa-15-parity-approximate-degree:
## Statement

For $N\ge1$, define $\mathrm{PARITY}_N(x)=|x|\pmod 2$. For every $0\le\epsilon<1/2$,
$$\widetilde{\deg}_{\epsilon}(\mathrm{PARITY}_N;\{0,1\}^N)=N,$$
and every local bit-query algorithm computing parity with error at most $\epsilon$ uses at least $\lceil N/2\rceil$ queries.
